{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham has the lowest Success rate (0.273) and the highest Time-to-Target (4.68 s), indicating poorest task performance without stimulation",
    "Combined stimulation yields the highest Success rate (0.780) and fastest Time-to-Target (2.56 s), with the largest sample size (n=48,846)",
    "Bright Visual Only achieves comparable Success (0.785) to Combined with slightly slower Time-to-Target (2.61 s), despite having the smallest sample (n=3,323)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance: Success rates of 0.673 and 0.685, Time-to-Target of 3.14 s and 3.05 s respectively",
    "Path Efficiency follows the same rank order as Success: Combined (0.502) ≈ Bright Visual Only (0.504) > Dim Visual Only (0.434) ≈ ICMS Only (0.432) > Sham (0.308)",
    "Average Speed is highest for Combined (12.83) and Bright Visual Only (12.68), intermediate for ICMS Only (12.04) and Dim Visual Only (11.97), and lowest for Sham (10.74)",
    "Angular Dispersion (AD) is highest in Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387), intermediate in ICMS Only (0.354) and Dim Visual Only (0.336), and lowest in Sham (0.236)",
    "Paradoxically, higher AD correlates with better performance: successful paradigms show more angular dispersion in movement trajectories"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined (0.780) shows a 2.85-fold difference, the largest effect across any variable",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68 s) is 1.83× slower than Combined (2.56 s), representing a 2.12 s absolute difference",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) shows a 63% relative deficit",
    "The bimodal pattern: Combined and Bright Visual Only cluster together as high-performing, while Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only cluster as intermediate, with Sham as clear outlier",
    "AD shows an inverse relationship to typical motor performance metrics: better-performing paradigms have higher AD, suggesting AD may reflect exploratory behavior or trajectory complexity rather than error"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Multimodal stimulation (Combined) and unimodal bright visual stimulation produce equivalent and superior navigation performance, suggesting that visual cues—particularly high-contrast ones—are the primary driver of task success. ICMS alone provides modest benefit over sham, while dim visual cues are similarly limited. The elevated angular dispersion in successful conditions likely reflects active exploration and course correction rather than disorientation, as it co-occurs with high success rates, fast completion times, and efficient paths. Sham conditions produce stereotyped, low-dispersion movements that are slow and unsuccessful, indicating a lack of effective strategy rather than mere motor deficit. These findings suggest that sensory augmentation, especially visual, enhances spatial navigation by enabling dynamic trajectory adjustment.",
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in sample sizes: Combined (48,846) versus Bright Visual Only (3,323) and Sham (3,505) limits confidence in comparisons involving smaller groups",
    "No statistical testing reported (e.g., ANOVA, post-hoc tests, confidence intervals); observed differences are descriptive only",
    "Cross-sectional summary statistics preclude inference about within-subject effects or learning trajectories",
    "Missing information on experimental design: randomization, block structure, and whether mice experienced multiple paradigms",
    "AD interpretation is ambiguous without validation against known behavioral constructs—higher values may indicate exploration, error, or task-specific strategy",
    "No correction for multiple comparisons or family-wise error rate in descriptive comparisons",
    "Extreme maximum values (Time-to-Target max=201.39, Path Efficiency max=29.82) suggest outliers or data quality issues not addressed in filtering"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression with Mouse as random intercept to account for repeated measures and individual variability, followed by planned contrasts comparing each active stimulation condition against Sham and against each other. Compute Cohen's d or Hedges' g effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals to quantify practical significance. Perform residual diagnostics to assess influence of extreme outliers on Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target. Finally, visualize interaction effects between stimulation paradigm and potential covariates (e.g., trial number, session) to assess whether performance differences are stable or modulated by experience."
}
